# Results — Study 159 (Presidential-Party) on real Shiller monthly tape

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). One data series —
Shiller S&P 500 **Real Price** (CPI-adjusted, log-returns), 1927-2023 — labelled by the
party of the sitting US president using the hardcoded `PRESIDENTS` table in
[`presidential_party/data.py`](../presidential_party/data.py). As-of **2026-06-15**.
Content fingerprint: `6c60cf65dd4c`.*

## Data stamp

| Source | Rows | Date range | Fingerprint |
|---|---|---|---|
| Shiller S&P 500 real price (parquet) | 1,160 months | 1927-02 → 2023-09 | `6c60cf65dd4c` |

Party coverage: **607 Democrat months** (8 terms) and **553 Republican months** (9 terms).
Presidential terms from the hardcoded table in `data.py` (see source comments for citations).

## Headline statistics (full sample 1927-2023)

### Per-party monthly real returns

| Party | n (months) | n (terms) | Mean (bps/month) | Mean (%/yr) | HAC t-stat |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| **Democrat** | 607 | 8 | **+43.84** | **+5.26** | +2.22 |
| **Republican** | 553 | 9 | **+5.37** | **+0.64** | +0.22 |
| **Unconditional** | 1,160 | 17 | **+25.50** | **+3.06** | — |

Note: the Democrat HAC t = +2.22 tests *'is D mean non-zero?'*, not *'is D > R?'* — it
inflates the apparent significance by ignoring the Republican baseline entirely.

### D-minus-R gap and inference

| Test | Statistic | Notes |
|---|--:|---|
| Raw gap (monthly) | **+38.46 bps/month** | = +4.62%/yr annualised |
| Welch t (monthly observations) | **+1.45** | 607 + 553 obs; not significant (|t| < 2) |
| HAC t (OLS dummy, Newey-West) | **+0.61** | autocorrelation-robust; even less significant |
| Block-permutation p (term-level) | **0.317** | shuffles 17 terms; consistent with chance |

The Welch t treats 1,160 monthly observations as independent. The block-permutation test
at the term level — where the real degrees of freedom live — gives p = 0.317, far from
any conventional significance threshold.

## Sub-sample robustness

| Period | n months | n terms | Gap (%/yr) | Welch t | HAC t | Perm p |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| Full (1927-2023) | 1,160 | 17 | +4.62 | +1.45 | +0.61 | 0.317 |
| Pre-war (1927-1952) | 311 | 4 | +10.72 | +0.78 | +0.40 | 1.000 |
| Post-war (1953-2023) | 849 | 14 | +4.58 | +1.58 | +0.61 | 0.356 |

The pre-war subsample (4 terms: Coolidge, Hoover, FDR×2) has n = 4 terms and a
perm p = 1.00 — the block shuffler cannot find an ordering more extreme than the observed
because there are only C(4,2) = 6 distinct permutations. The gap in the post-war era is
similar in magnitude (+4.58%/yr) but no more significant.

## The confound — Depression/WWII

The pre-war Republican terms (Coolidge 1927-29, Hoover 1929-33) include the 1929 Crash
and the Great Depression. The pre-war Democratic terms (FDR 1933-1945) include the
post-Depression recovery and WWII war-economy boom. The −60 bps/month Republican pre-war
average vs +29 bps/month Democratic pre-war average reflects **crisis timing**, not
party policy. This is the central confound identified by Blinder & Watson (2016, AER).

## Synthetic positive control

A planted Democrat premium is recoverable in the synthetic tape when it is large enough:

| Planted premium (bps/month) | Observed gap (bps/month) | Welch t | Perm p | Certified? |
|---|--:|--:|--:|:--:|
| 0 (null) | ~−7 | ~−0.28 | ~0.80 | no |
| 25 | ~+18 | ~+0.69 | ~0.54 | no |
| 50 | ~+43 | ~+1.66 | ~0.15 | no |
| 100 | ~+93 | ~+3.60 | ~0.003 | yes |
| 200 | ~+193 | ~+7.48 | ~0.000 | yes |

The real observed gap of +38 bps/month maps between the 25 and 50 bps/month planted-
premium range — clearly in the "not certified at the term level" zone.

## Verdict

- **Signal — WEAK.** The raw gap (+4.62%/yr) is large by market-anomaly standards but
  lives on only 17 presidential terms (8 D, 9 R). Welch t = +1.45 (monthly) and
  block-permutation p = 0.317 (term-level) do not clear the inference bar. The HAC
  correction further reduces the t-stat to +0.61. The effect is consistent with being
  entirely explained by business-cycle timing (Blinder & Watson 2016).
- **Tradability — MIRAGE.** Party composition is observable only after the election,
  which markets price immediately. No advance signal exists; and even if the effect were
  real, one data-point per 4-year term makes accumulating evidence across a human lifetime
  essentially impossible.
- **Tiny-n — BUSTED.** With 17 effective observations at the term level, no t-stat or
  p-value from monthly observations certifies causality. The Depression/WWII coincidence
  with Democratic administrations (FDR, 1933-1945) accounts for the bulk of the headline.
